reasoning_details.text:
I'm going through the first screenshot, overview-1440: the header, stats row, two amber-bordered notices, chip row, filters, explanatory text, and table. The Qwen rows show a "Recorded" chip with no projection marker at row level, and the column header reads "Requested envelope: 0 / 3 batches." So the projection labeling is missing at the cell level, and Qwen cells look the same as recorded ones.

Looking at the Qwen and Gemini detail pages, the "Response envelope" label sits apart from its value on mobile, and "No projection recorded" is ambiguous enough to read like a missing record. On the headline stats, the chip counts change under the filter while the summary figures above stay global, which could confuse someone scanning the page.

I'm noting that the chip row doesn't say it reflects the current selection, which is a minor gap. The "Divergent" and "Observed disagreement" chips share the same red styling, so a reader could mix up the counts of 1 and 3. The explanatory line calling it "three-way divergence" may be misleading, since P013 splits 2 to 1 rather than all three reviewers differing, so "divergent" alone, scoped to complete triads, would be clearer.

The mobile inspector's "Response envelope" label sits apart from its value, which reads as a moderate craft issue, and the small link targets are only just adequate. The matrix itself isn't visible at mobile width in these screenshots, so that's a gap I can't assess yet. The desktop table also leaves a lot of empty space, with the "Requested envelope: 0 / 3 batches" header in tiny text serving as the only matrix-level cue for Qwen's raw output.

I'm also weighing the frozen draft label column, where translation rows say "No semantic gold assigned" and verification rows show "supported" or "not established" under "Frozen draft label," which avoids calling anything gold. I'm now checking how the rest of that column's wording holds up.

I'm checking whether the frozen draft label column's wording overstates things, since "No semantic gold assigned" could suggest the verification rows do have gold labels. Then I'm questioning whether the family overlap disclosure appears anywhere in these screenshots, which I can't confirm from what's visible.

I'm noting that the family-overlap disclosure isn't visible in these frames, so I can't confirm it either way. The "12 incomplete" in the stats and the chip count of 12 items are separate units that happen to match, since each affected item is missing one judgment.

I'm weighing whether the Craft and Functionality scores should be 1 or 2, since the mobile matrix can't be checked from these frames and the inspector label wrapping is a real but small flaw. I'm leaning toward a PASS with advisory fixes, though I want to make sure that call holds up against the rating rules.

I'm weighing the Craft and Functionality scores, leaning toward 2 for both, since the projection labeling is handled in the inspector, header, and caption, though the Qwen cell-level marker is still a priority fix.

I'm listing the remaining fixes: a cell-level projection marker for the Qwen rows, separating the mobile "Response envelope" label from its value, and renaming "Three-way divergence" to match the complete-triad chip. I'm also weighing whether the "gold" wording wrongly implies verification items have gold labels.
